# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Chance's Claim for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## The Name Nobody agrees who Chance was. The survey office says it is only a catalogue name. The old drillers say he was a prospector who staked the first claim on LV-522 and never lived to cash it. Either way, the name stuck, and most people here will tell you it fits.
## The Charter LV-522 was settled for its ore. Weyland-Yutani holds the charter, the mines, the landing pads and most of the payroll, and the colony is run by a Company administrator rather than an elected council. The terms are posted at the [netlink="Colony Administration" link="admin.colony.gov/charter"], and they are worth reading twice.
## The Processor The air on LV-522 is still being made. The atmospheric processor beyond the colony streets has run since the first crews landed, its reactors feeding the filtration halls day and night. Reactor technicians and filtration crews are the best paid people in town who never touch ore, and a rumour of a fault out there is the one thing that can empty the bar.
## The Blocks - [bold]A-Block[/bold] holds the operations centre, the corporate offices, security, medical, the kitchens and most of the shared dorms. - [bold]B-Block[/bold] holds the hydroponics bays and the bar. - [bold]C-Block[/bold] holds the mining offices, cargo, the garage and the casino.
Between them run open streets and the container yard. The windbreakers along the edge of town were raised against the wind and rain that never really stop. The landing sign by the pad has been repainted more times than anyone can count.
## The Crime Wave Money came in with the ore, and so did people who wanted it without the digging. Through 2182 the colony has seen protection rackets, missing cargo, robberies on the night streets and debts settled outside the casino. Company Security says it is in hand. A response force has now been sent anyway.
The Herald writes down who was hurt, who was paid and who looked away. That archive is open to anyone who asks.
